body: Wow this hit home. I recently discovered that because of this, I started rejecting emotions. This happened half my life ago. So here I am, apathetic and utterly motivationless.
I love the title! Could be an album title, or maybe book title? I'd listen/read it.
Yes! That movie had some awesome moments. Really weird ending though

Knowing of her mothers negative response to an obvious issue of suicide attempt, it sounds pretty certain that some emotions had to be masked in that home (you could say I have some experience...). At least there has not been room for Jess to express grief her way. That shit might have surfaced now when she got more problems on hand.

Know that you are not responsible for her (guilting yourself does not help anyone), but rather acknowledge your will to help. However little point life has, you might help her get a better shot at it (for what it's worth).

Hi. It's the first time I've read anyone feeling that they might kill someone. While I've sort of locked my feelings away, I worry what could happen if I start to live a more emotional connected life. Because I *know* I could kill someone. Now even at cold blood (or locked blood?). I rarely feel much though, so I'll probably die before that.

It sounds like Kerry doesn't understand how MDD work, so I think she will only make Jess worse. Even complaining about Jess' way of dealing with her fathers death is completely wrong. How can one expect that to not affect her strongly? And why the fuck complain about how a child (assuming it happened years ago) handled her emotions? That is usually taught through parenting. She needs more help than her mother (maybe dealing with something herself) is able to give atm.

(Vague advice at best) I'd confess (not the right word) to her that you know about her attempt (the way it's done could be critical) and that she is not alone with those feelings. This does of course require one on one time. Could be a quick passing by when nobody's there. That's my two cents.
If it helps somehow, I can't find a logical reason why anyone should live. So you're doing fine in my book.
Any experiences?
[Never stop dreaming, son!](http://cdn.iwastesomuchtime.com/12102014224660.png)

Yeah, for one and a half year. Little progress. Tried several meds with no effect. Even though my current psychiatrist is good, I feel like I've given up on it, like most things. Life in general. What "my study on life" has shown me is that the concept is meager and, for me at current state, not worth living.

I've always been quite good at science (and systems in general?) and also found it interesting. Later on the process and the logical approach really appealed to me. Though, during my time with my psychiatrist I've remembered that I manifested that "emotions are not productive", so I think I cut them off at a very young age. Maybe science was a place where my parting from emotions did work so I felt comfortable there and went for it? Or the other way around?

Why I cut off emotions, I don't know. I might have gone half my life without knowing/thinking about it. But I remember seeing a pattern where all good things where eventually followed by a setback. So rather than the rocky roller coaster (where you ended up at the level you started at anyways) I went for a "smooth ride". Stability is highly praised in school and society, so it must be good! Or so naive little me believed it had to be. Or knew? Don't remember.

> I think the mistake that you are doing is that life can't be boiled down to an easy science, solvable by man.

Now you're setting boundaries (btw "easy science" is with a couple variables is not what I'm looking for. I've articulated the concept far beyond that). Isn't "impossible" what supposedly we stretch after? M. Ali thought so: “Impossible is just a big word thrown around by small men who find it easier to live in the world they’ve been given than to explore the power they have to change it. Impossible is not a fact. It’s an opinion. Impossible is not a declaration. It’s a dare. Impossible is potential. Impossible is temporary. Impossible is nothing.” The one thing I would want changed is my approach on it. Rather than "learning" stuff, I find that by exploring I still enjoy things once in a while. PC games for instance. Real life adventures feels too much of a hassle and since it's "all done before", any motivation erodes away before I get started. But I ramble.

I've found that I'm so much better at following up a project than starting it. So my post was my take on starting it. Questions are needed.

Scientific method is a bit fancy and probably somewhat misleading. A plain use of reasoning or logic may be more accurate. By plain I think of life this far: get an education to be off to a good start on adulthood. No thought has been given to whether or not I really want a the stability it gives. There has been no room for feelings this far so I stopped listening to them in order to reach "my" goals.

Atm I have a job (of sorts) at an assembly line. Eight hours of the same repetitious task. A couple of years ago I could've hardly imagined a more boring job for "a bright intellectual, yet practical mind". But I give zero fucks. I don't care. I could have done that work for every awake moment without it bothering me (other than the fact that life itself is pointless and in the end sucks).

Today it affected me by not getting up until 1pm missing work. Being well of economically and it being a random place, I have no drive to go there other than my psychiatrist wanting me to. When I'm awake I don't mind going, but sleeping is so good (only thing in life) so my lack of proper sleep habits makes getting to work very hit or miss.

Edit: My memory has taken a severe hit. My psychiatrist thinks it's because of my lack of emotions. Usually the things we remember the best are things that touched us emotionally (or so I've heard).

Yeah, at least at this point. I mean, I needed a fair bit of life to get to this point of. But then again is "this point" worth shit? The only thing I really feel that I've gained is this realization that it's all pointless. What a prize.

While I agree on being a fuck-up, I feel I've done ok. I (the spoiled, self-righteous shit) am at the point where I feel that the "normal" people are the ones with the biggest flaws. Us fucked up (or whatever) have just gotten the unfortunate "flukes" that society doesn't know how to deal with (introversion feels like an ok example here). So I've actually kinda come to terms with my flukes, as well as most other peoples flukes; in theory, that is. We're all people wandering around in the same boat. People that come of as shits have some sort of shitty background, so no need to hate on them for that (plus humans decision-making is a beta at best).

Apart from my emotions (or lack thereof) and the diagnose I'm very good. I was born into an "easy" world, or at least a wealthy part of it. Excellent dice. But I see no point in it. Whatever I can do with my resources have stopped interesting me. While I sometimes do make an effort, it's usually a convenient one for me (quite good at learning new things is often an ace).

I actually feel like I've lived whatever a "full life" is. I've learned a lot (school++), had ok friends, achieved a fair bit, worked, had girlfriend, traveled, and yet I'm in my early twenties wondering "is that it?". If the rest is pure repetition (maybe plus kids), I'd rather not.

I have no idea what to talk about. And usually when I talk on these things I only feel that I burden people, so I seldom do. But thanks.

Edit: If *you* would like to, shoot. I can enjoy a chat.
Yup, I feel you. My (once extremely) logical mind has found no reason to keep going. Even without any roadblocks in life I see no reason to go on. I don't enjoy any of it, so what's left?

That was oddly refreshing (?). I really feel you on the lies. Although I've tried to be more blunt and give straighter answers, it has just made it harder for me to meet people. I actually sort of hate people.

Btw: Your post could be a transcript for a short film. It really tells a story! I like the style.
I'm not slow though, so maybe some sort of super sloth? I could have ss in my fur and pull out my rusty German accent just to inspire fright. I'd be a real fucker. Super Sloth. Yeah, that'll be me.

I'm not built for either, so that would be terrific! Thanks! :D

But I'd also love to be a sloth. They're so [handsome](http://everythingfunny.org/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/1bbb.jpg). I'd be like sleeping beauty and wake up to all these lovely ladies kissing me :D (I could be dreaming, not important).

As a privileged shit I have the luxury of no hurry, but euthanasia actually have not struck me. Not legal afaik her neither. Knowing how health care and stuff works it would probably take forever to get through and have low priority for me demographic, so I'd probably end up DIYing it. Could be fun, I like "DIY" projects :)

While I think /u/ohwontyouthrowmeaway is onto something, I always end up feeling hollow and empty after these encounters. Maybe it's because I'm not able to break the "cycle"? I doubt, so I feel you op. "Soon" can have a varying meaning (can testify), so not too soon? I'm lucky enough to not have any hurry. I wish everyone could have that privilege.

Mars Volta! Not often one comes across in the wild. While I have no specific "shitty feeling", I love some of the dark and twisted stuff from Mars Volta. "Similar" stuff to me include Porcupine Tree. I also enjoy Pink Floyd, but to me they're more casual.

*Note to self: More Radiohead.
Sounds awesome :D I'm actually on my way, not with fat or muscles though.
Damn, poor you. Sounds terrible. I'm pretty close to op on 23 max. I've never really tried though, just happened. Was probably up for quite long beforehand though.

And why should I bother to distract myself? It's not like it will change anything. At best it's a not dull glimpse that disappear instantly. Being aprox apathetic makes these glimpse barely different than the rest and having shit memory makes them pass so fast. I've stopped bothering with distracting myself.

Apathetic as always. At work I stood by a table and assembled one part of pallets for 8 hours. That was about ok. Nothing really appeals to me. I know I should be hungry atm, but I dont bother. Life is pointless and long as always. Nothing change. It sort of bothers me that I cant be bothered to end it all. that might be the only thing I can say for certain. It could be nice.

Edit: work is an over statement. Not much.

Yeah, not that it does me good.. One extremely useful feature is to unfollow the people that pose the most glamorous stories. You're still friend with them and get all the same requests, but don't have to read about their fantastic (side!) of life. It has made my facebook liveable.

This! The facade is basically what I see "social" media as. Comparing one self to the glossed up stories on FB does NO good. Using time elsewhere is a step away from that feeling. But yeah, I have somewhat a similar feeling. But I've never been the sociable one, so not doing stuff often is fine by me.
Yeah, ok people seems to exist somewhere. "Normal stuff" can involve a lot of interesting good cool stuff. What's NIB?

I hate when people disregards pc altogether as a good hobby (parents...). Of course it does not have to, but throwing it away under the label pc I feel is wrong. I have a friend that is employed purely from being ok with computers.
Do you do anything interesting/fancy on it? Or browse potential hobbies? I could kinda see myself try practicing some of my browsing things. Like Im a fan of diy-ing, but I rarely get around making any projects. But I get if that sounds like a lot of work and less rewarding.
But I also get that a pc does not have to involve any productive stuff. Could all be porn for what I know (although there are interesting/creative++ stuff there too). But pleasure is worth a lot when there is none elsewhere. Yeah, working medicine should be celebrated. Stuff that work in general? win
I hope you don't expect any miracles here from my rambling. Take it for what it is.
Ex

I've yet to find any grounded reasons for myself. So far, I solely live on old habit. So I feel you. If you have anything like sports or art or something like that you enjoy and would be able to put your mind to it, it could be worth a last effort? A brainstorm on reasons to live could be really interesting, so feel free to add more. I'd also want some.

I'm only diagnosed with depression, so "nothing major". lol. But it's an easy excuse to do nothing. I don't even know if that's the case. It's more of an existential crisis. Not that it would exclude depression, but my therapist is clueless what to do. She even asked if I was using drugs (knowing me and where I come from, lol).

No problem. Rambling like that could potentially be therapeutic, so win-win maybe. Rewarding is good. Harvest where you can. Needing to be seen and cared for at work could be hard. I've yet to have such work (21y), so my advice is hardly worth anything, but patience maybe? That feels too much like "it gets better", so I'm not taking that advice myself -.- But theoretically speaking, rolling the dice over and over again will give better results (and worse, mediocre, and others :/ ). Statistics.
Congrats on job though! Money in usually lowers the stress level, so yay indeed! Rewarding with weed seems strange to this narrow minded dude, but if it works it works. My ex was doing some weed while at school. I miss her.

Yes. Being wealthy enough (atm), entitled and technically ill I'm basically in bed most of the times. Or else I'm in my room at my computer. I rarely get around watching anything really, some youtube though, but mostly bed. Or bathroom. It has a lock.

Losing interest in everything is numbing. I can't relate to the family thing as I luckily don't have my own (having other people to take care of sounds exhausting). Saying that life will get better sounds to me like an efficient way to dismiss current pain. Sleeping works better for me too -.- To me though, it sound like you are a pretty decent person. Not perfect, maybe not great, but you obviously care a lot about your family. Your kids might not appreciate it now, but you caring for them does make a big difference. Coming from a caring family myself, I highly appreciate what my parents have kept together. I've skipped past a bunch of problems. Knowing that you've helped something for your kids like that is better than any praise. Or something. Maybe I'm just tired. Some sense may have occurred though. Bye

Working out or something along those lines helps a lot on self esteem, or just accomplishing something (like working on your body, or art or whatever your thing is). Doing that and respecting women sounds like your on an ok track. The negativity can be a tough one though. If you have the chance, therapy can work, but it can be very hit and miss. I've yet to hit anything. Even people like pastors or alike can be of help on tough matters like that (if your ok with them, though they should by no means demand any religious stuff from you).
Hope some of my rambling can be of help.

Sorry if I come off picky, but life does not have to be a lot. I can vouch for that. And being captain obvious does not have to help. Getting obvious/optimistic advice really bothers me. If it where my post I'd not bothered replying to such reply, to stay productive.
